Lysosomal storage umbrella; skeletal disease, neurologic impairment and corneal/retinal disease are common across major subtypes, estimated >=30% each; subtype variability is substantial.

Corticospinal degeneration and peripheral neuropathy; urinary urgency reflects neurologic dysfunction, while amyotrophy does not establish primary muscle damage.

Fluke infection umbrella; hepatic, pulmonary and intestinal locations vary by parasite subtype, with no single anatomical organ established across most patients.

Skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae, metaphyses, hips and ossification; no qualifying extraskeletal organ damage is established.

Intellectual disability and dystonia define the syndrome; spasticity and dysarthria are neurologic, while fixed contractures lack a qualifying frequency.
Reproductive sex-cord/stromal neoplasm; hormonal dysfunction is subtype-dependent and is not established across this umbrella.
Craniosynostosis, pulmonary valve stenosis and intellectual disability/ventriculomegaly define syndrome; ectopic anus is also a defining feature, qualifying GI by diagnostic criteria.
Obesity establishes a metabolic phenotype; short stature alone does not establish skeletal disease. Additional defining organ abnormalities are not supplied.

Proline metabolism disorder; seizures and developmental/intellectual impairment annotated 80-99%, despite often benign course. Renal insufficiency 5-29% excluded.
